_V3_REFRAME_NOTE: The -11.4% prompt-4 decode-only delta below was originally framed as evidence that MTP is intrinsically negative across hardware classes. After the v3 clean A/B retest (2026-04-26, results/mtp_v3_clean_ab_*.json) found MTP k=1 is +27.5% faster on the same 2x RTX 3090 hardware once `--no-enable-prefix-caching` is set, this A100 -11.4% is reframed as the **prefix-cache-ON regime A100 NVLink datapoint** (this Modal run kept `--enable-prefix-caching` ON, see serve_flags below). vllm #38182 reports MTP drops prefix-cache hit rate ~92%->~71% on the same model class, which is the most parsimonious explanation for the cache-ON A100 regression. Whether A100 NVLink with prefix-cache OFF would also flip positive (matching the 3090 v3 result) is the OPEN follow-up — Modal credits permitting, a v3-equivalent A100 retest with cache OFF is the natural next step. Until that retest is run, do NOT cite this -11.4% as evidence MTP is hardware-class-independent negative.
_WARNING: The auto-computed `nvlink.comparison.mean_delta_pct: +14.3%` is a MEASUREMENT ARTIFACT, not a real MTP speedup. 4 of 5 prompts early-stopped on A100 (vs all 5 hitting max_tokens=200 on 3090), so prefill overhead distorts the per-prompt tok/s mean. The valid same-hardware A/B comparison on prompt 4 (only prompt that ran long under no-MTP) shows MTP at -11.4% decode-rate. See `analysis_corrected` for full per-prompt breakdown. (Note: this -11.4% is now read as the prefix-cache-ON regime A100 datapoint per the _V3_REFRAME_NOTE above, not as evidence MTP is intrinsically negative.)

vs_2x_3090_baseline.note: Cross-hardware comparison disentangles two variables: (1) GPU memory bandwidth (3090 GDDR6X 936 GB/s vs A100 HBM2e 2 TB/s), and (2) TP allreduce interconnect (3090 PCIe ~16 GB/s vs A100 NVLink ~600 GB/s). The 4-condition matrix isolates each.
vs_2x_3090_baseline._WARNING_3090_published_confound: The published 3090 -12% delta is NOT a clean A/B test. Per `results/mtp_speculative_decoding.json`, the 3090 baseline used `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --max-num-seqs 8`, but the 3090 MTP run used `0.80 / 2` (originally chosen for OOM headroom that turned out unnecessary). The -12% therefore conflates MTP-method impact with serve-config impact. A 3090 re-run with matched flags is needed for clean cross-hardware comparison; the A100 numbers above were collected with consistent 0.90/8 across both no-MTP and MTP runs (clean A/B).

comparison._WARNING_DO_NOT_CITE: These auto-computed numbers are measurement artifact. Reasoning: tok/s = ct/elapsed_s includes prefill (TTFT). When 4 of 5 prompts early-stop at ct < max_tokens, prefill overhead amplifies into the rate, distorting the mean across prompts of unequal length. The +14.3% mean_delta_pct is dominated by no-MTP prompt 2 stalling at 43 tok/s (likely transient Modal cold-container hiccup) — not by MTP speeding things up. The 0.4x stdev_blowup_factor reflects different early-stop patterns between no-MTP and MTP runs (sampling-path divergence under temp=0.5/seed=42), not lower variance from MTP itself. Use `analysis_corrected.per_prompt` instead.

analysis_corrected.method: Same-hardware same-prompt-index A/B comparison. Note: identical seed=42 + temperature=0.5 produces different completion_tokens between no-MTP and MTP runs (because spec-decode alters RNG-consumption path), so per-prompt tok/s comparison is bounded by sampling-path divergence — only valid when both runs produce comparable ct.

per_prompt_table.verdict: DIVERGENT_CT — both early-stopped but at very different lengths (45 vs 67). TTFT-dominated; raw rates not directly comparable.

OUTLIER_NO_MTP — no-MTP took 1.86s for 80 tokens (43 tok/s), 3x slower than no-MTP prompts 3-4 (122-128 tok/s). Almost certainly a transient stall (NCCL warmup, prefix-cache miss on cold container, or first-call jit). DROP this prompt from cross-method analysis. This single outlier dominates the misleading +14.3% mean_delta_pct.
VALID_COMPARISON — similar ct (138 vs 134, within 3%), MTP elapsed +7% with 4 fewer tokens. TTFT-adjusted (TTFT≈80ms): no-MTP 130.5 tok/s, MTP 117.4 tok/s, delta -10.1%.

BEST_APPLES_TO_APPLES — same elapsed wall-time, no-MTP produced 21 more tokens. TTFT-adjusted (TTFT≈80ms): no-MTP 134.8 tok/s, MTP 119.5 tok/s, delta -11.4%. This delta is robust to TTFT estimate (varies <0.2pp across TTFT ∈ [0, 200ms]).
TTFT_DOMINATED — both early-stopped extremely short (19, 21 tokens). Total elapsed is mostly prefill+TTFT, not decode. Not informative.

analysis_corrected.honest_delta_basis: Mean of valid-comparison prompts 3 and 4 (TTFT-adjusted, TTFT=80ms). Excludes outlier prompt 2 and TTFT-dominated/divergent prompts 1, 5.
analysis_corrected.headline_finding: On 2x A100-80GB SXM4 with NVLink (HBM2e 2 TB/s + NVLink 300 GB/s), vLLM 0.19.1 MTP k=1 does NOT solve the regression seen on 2x 3090 PCIe (GDDR6X 936 GB/s + PCIe 16 GB/s). Decode-rate decline is similar magnitude (~-11%). This is the FIRST clean cross-hardware A/B (A100 used matched serve flags both runs). Conclusion: 'GDDR6X memory bandwidth' is RULED OUT as the sole bottleneck; 'MoE × spec-decode structural conflict' is the dominant mechanism. NVLink also rules out 'TP allreduce on PCIe' as the sole cause.

caveats: N=1 trial per condition. Run-to-run cold-start variance NOT characterized. Prompt-2 outlier in no-MTP run shows N=1 is fragile.

Cross-hardware sampling-path divergence: identical seed=42 + temperature=0.5 produces different completion_tokens on 3090 (all 5 prompts hit max_tokens=200) vs A100 (45/80/138/200/19). Cause: floating-point non-associativity in TP=2 allreduce reductions on PCIe (3090) vs NVLink (A100) yields slightly different logits → temperature 0.5 sampling lands on different tokens at top-k boundaries → cascading EOS-time divergence. Expected behavior, not a bug, but invalidates naive cross-hardware mean tok/s comparison.

Prefill (TTFT) not measured separately — `tok/s = ct / elapsed_s` rolls TTFT into the rate. Per-prompt comparison requires TTFT-adjustment or prompts that don't early-stop. The headline -11.4% on prompt 4 IS robust to TTFT assumption because both A and B share the same TTFT for the same prompt content.

3090 published -12% delta has its own confound: baseline used gpu-memory-utilization=0.90/max-num-seqs=8, MTP used 0.80/2 (originally for OOM headroom that proved unnecessary per `results/mtp_speculative_decoding.json` boot_findings). Need 3090 rerun with matched flags for fully clean cross-hardware comparison.

Modal A100 image cached after first run. Boot time (528.4s no-MTP, 510.3s MTP) reflects fresh CUDA-graph capture each container restart — not steady-state in-process behavior. The cooler 510s second-run hints at HF Volume warmth, not MTP speedup.
what_this_does_NOT_test: PCIe-forced TP=2 on A100 (would require `--four-condition` re-run with NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1) — disentangles HBM2e-bandwidth from NVLink-interconnect contributions
Single-card on Blackwell GDDR7 (5090) — would isolate pure memory-BW axis from TP/interconnect axes entirely
EAGLE-3 with CUDA graphs (vLLM Model Runner V2) — different draft architecture; not evaluated here
Higher concurrency (max-num-seqs > 8) — MTP may amortize verify cost across requests
Different MTP num_speculative_tokens (k=2, k=4) — only k=1 tested
